claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53.
The quasi-static yield strength of the starting alloy is 786 MPa.
The quasi-static compressive strength of the starting alloy is 1314 MPa.
The quasi-static fracture strain of the starting alloy is 13.5%.
The proposed intervention adds 0.5 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles with diameters of 5–20 nm.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark-plasma sintering will produce a uniform Y2O3 dispersion in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The resulting Y2O3 particles will have approximately 100 nm spacing and occur both at grain boundaries and within grains of an approximately 1 µm-grained matrix.
The Y2O3 particles will provide Orowan strengthening.
Dislocation–particle interactions will increase the strain-hardening rate.
The increased strain-hardening rate will delay deformation localization and adiabatic shear banding.
Particle strengthening will raise the critical strain for shear-band initiation under adiabatic heating.
At strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1, the intervention will increase dynamic yield strength by about 15%, to approximately 900 MPa.
At strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1, the intervention will increase peak compressive strength by about 20%, to approximately 1600 MPa.
At strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1, the intervention will increase dynamic fracture strain by about 50%, from approximately 5% to approximately 7.5%.
The intervention will increase shear-band onset strain by approximately 50%.
The intervention will increase impact energy absorption by approximately 25% relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy is expected to have dynamic yield strength of approximately 780 MPa, compressive strength of approximately 1300 MPa, and dynamic fracture strain of approximately 5%.
The dynamic-compression prediction applies at room temperature under adiabatic loading at strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1.
The impact prediction applies to steel-projectile velocities of 200–300 m/s.
The prediction is bounded to tests with a maximum temperature rise below 500 °C.
